title: The Chaldean Oracles, Vol. 1
author: G. R. S. Mead
description: The Chaldean Oracles, Volume 1, by G. R. S. Mead (London: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1908), Volume VIII of the 'Echoes from the Gnosis' series. The Chaldean Oracles are fragments of a second-century CE hexameter poem attributed to Julian the Chaldean and his son Julian the Theurgist, which the later Neoplatonists Porphyry, Iamblichus and Proclus treated as divine revelation. In this first volume Mead introduces the Oracles, their history and their importance for theurgy, then presents and comments on fragments concerning the Paternal Depth and the Father, the Paternal Intellect, the triads, the Great Mother or Hecate as cosmic soul, the Iynges, the Connectors and Teletarchs, the Empyrean, ethereal and material worlds, and the 'flower of mind'. Mead's accessible introduction made these texts known to Theosophical and esoteric readers and to modern ritual magic.
